findings.where: The blue 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' band right under the first screen: its white 'Subscribe' button (desktop-02 top, phone-01)
findings.fault: The Subscribe button is a link to #subscribe, and the parts map shows no form, email field or other control anywhere on the page. A visitor who clicks it lands on the band they are already looking at, and nothing happens. It is a dead action dressed as the page's strongest button, a white fill on a full-width blue field. It also sets up a second competing call to action straight after the hero's one action, 'Write to me directly'.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who wants Mark's briefings clicks, nothing happens, and they decide the site is broken. That undercuts the trust the hero just built. The founder ruled one direct, personal way to reach Mark, and the research asks for one action. A second, louder button that does nothing works against both.

findings.where: First screen, top bar (desktop-01, phone-01): only 'Mark M. Moseley' and the MMM Infra mark, no other navigation
findings.fault: The first screen has no navigation. The brief's first-screen scope starts with 'nav', and the page's own palette table assigns 'mist on slate' to 'nav links', but none are built. From the hero, a visitor cannot reach Mark's articles, his talks and papers, or anything about him. The only link up there is the logo, which goes to #top, the screen they are already on.
findings.who_objects: A visitor from a development agency who wants to check Mark's record or read his PPP writing before writing to him finds no route to it. The homepage is meant to lead to the article and PDF pages, which the research calls 'the product', and here it leads nowhere.

findings.where: Article specimen, the blue-tinted lecture card 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge' with its download arrow and 'PDF' label (desktop-06, phone-04)
findings.fault: The card promises a file: a download arrow and the word 'PDF'. The parts map shows the whole card linking to #article, an in-page jump. Clicking 'PDF' downloads nothing. The card is also the only part of the page with a drop shadow and a raised, tinted surface, so its look claims a weight its action doesn't have.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants to save Mark's lecture to read later or pass on to colleagues clicks PDF, expects a download, and is moved around the page instead. The PDF list is meant to be the product, so the one sample of it should do what it says.

findings.where: The house blue used on static text: the 'PALETTE' eyebrow (desktop-02, phone-01) and the article list's numbers 1-3 (desktop-05, phone-04)
findings.fault: The specimen states the rule 'Grey for reading, blue only where something can be clicked', and blue is the link colour throughout. But the PALETTE label and the list numbers are blue and do nothing, so blue means 'link' in some places and 'decoration' in others. The PALETTE label is the only spaced-capitals label in blue; the other section labels ('Type pair', 'An article page', 'Motion sketch') are grey.
findings.who_objects: Angélique, who will add content following the rule the page states, gets two exceptions she can't explain. A reader who hovers or taps blue text expecting a link finds nothing.

findings.where: First screen, the lockup: 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The name and the mark are set as one lockup, split by a hairline. The mark is a link home and the name is static text, so half the lockup acts and the other half, which looks the same, does not.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who clicks the name to go home, as most sites let them, gets no response. Few would notice on a one-screen home, but it is the one place the name leads, as the founder asked.
